title: Predictive burst repair orchestration and tenant prioritization
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Multiple customer escalations in the last 72h surfaced a recurrent pattern: the dedicated autoscaler failed to replenish reserved pools under sustained microburst traffic, leading to tenant-visible 429s and graceful-degradation fallbacks. This ticket coordinates a short-term hotfix + mid-term resilience changes: fix the headroom accounting bug that mis-classified warmup credits, add per-tenant prioritization when headroom is scarce, and improve operator runbooks/dashboards for faster recovery. Scope covers Dedicated control-plane changes, autoscaler leader logic, and immediate customer-facing mitigations (fallback routing and quota adjustments).

root_cause: The autoscaler used an epoch-based warmup-credit accounting subsystem that mistakenly aggregated transient KV cache warmup tokens from preempted slots into tenant headroom. Under microburst patterns with many short-lived sessions, the aggregation logic double-counted warmup credits and suppressed scale-up signals for the reserved pool leader. This was exacerbated by a stale safety threshold in the leader derate function that assumed monotonic credit decay. Result: headroom appeared sufficient to the controller while real usable capacity was exhausted.
mitigation: Hotpatch v1: Fix warmup-credit aggregation to use per-slot decays instead of global summation and clamp negative deltas; deployed to canary and validated with traffic replay.
Operator mitigations: temporary increase to reserved-pool soft quotas for impacted tenants; manual rebalancing of warm pools to give breathing room for small tenants.
Fallback routing: expanded automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model variants for non-SLA traffic until rollout completes.
Communication: Affected customers received targeted status updates and recommended client-side retry/backoff tuning.
remediation_plan: 1) Immediate (this sprint): ship hotfix to full fleet with canary guard and 30-minute reconciliation checks. (Owner: Miguel)

2) Near-term (2 sprints): implement per-tenant prioritization policy when headroom < X% to avoid starving high-paying tenants; add admission-controller hooks to prefer VIP routes. (Owner: Capacity team)

3) Medium-term (quarter): rewrite headroom estimator to incorporate KV-cache decay models and sequence-length-aware forecasts; add predictive autoscaler signals from workload classifiers. (Owner: Autoscales & Forecasting)
4) Observability: add dedicated headroom-visibility dashboard with per-tenant and per-AZ heatmap, and an alert when headroom projection crosses tiered thresholds. (Owner: Observability)
5) Runbooks: publish a step-by-step runbook for reserved-pool underprovision events with playbook automations (auto-rollback, temporary quota bump, cross-pool failover). (Owner: SRE)
6) Postmortem: complete postmortem doc and SLA credit determinations after rollout is stable. (Owner: Incident Leader)
rollback_plan: If the hotfix increases error rates or causes leader flaps: 1) pause rollout; 2) rollback to previous runtime image using the orchestrator with automatic leader reconciliation; 3) re-enable manual mitigations (quota bump, fallback routing); 4) escalate to runtime-oncall for step debugging. Canary is instrumented to auto-abort rollout if 429s or leader-election anomalies spike beyond configured thresholds.
test_plan: Unit tests for warmup-credit aggregation and negative-delta clamping.
Integration tests: synthetic microburst replays with mixed short/long sessions to validate headroom projection.
Load test: staged canary under production-like traffic replays targeting 120% of observed burst peaks.
Chaos test: simulate preemption and leader failover while running the hotfix to ensure no split-brain credit state remains.
followups: Add tenant-priority simulation harness to the autoscaler testbed (ENG-208999 placeholder for follow-up ticket).
Formalize SLOs for reserved-pool headroom and include in Console's per-route dashboards.
Evaluate whether quantization/kv-cache eviction policies interact with headroom under high-KV workloads and propose mitigations.
Customer outreach: schedule QBR-style debriefs for the three largest impacted accounts and provide technical root cause writeup.
